ownership: Only ScreenPreviewCoordinator.kt, ScreenProjectionService.kt and the focused production-used pure JVM lifecycle seam/test were changed. Parent retains queue, policy, existing tests, builds and devices.

changes.change: Local Stop, remote Stop and authenticated protocol rejection now select and terminally invalidate the exact pending/running request under one coordinator lock. Cancellation, queue purge and native stop happen afterward. The pending-to-running gap and nullable-ID re-fetch are removed.

Issued launches remain outstanding after revocation until service delivery and release, or a known launch failure. Delivery registration is separate from capture authorization. Revoked deliveries are attached to service cleanup without obtaining projection. The service acknowledges all delivered tickets only after capture-thread release.

Resize publishes its new generation and cancels old active output before native surface/reader/display work. Response dispatch validity also checks the runtime service generation, closing the interval before coordinator publication.
projectionStopped(USER) now requests a peer stop notice. A remotely initiated Stop has already removed running before the service callback and therefore still produces no echo.
Completed/unissued/known-failed lifetime records retire immediately, without requiring a later awaitQuiescence call. No timer or deadline completes a lifecycle in place of release.

Foreground setup now shares the serial capture handler with acquisition and teardown, preventing foreground work after a parallel release. Capture-thread join retries interruption and restores the interrupt flag after cleanup instead of continuing as though the thread exited.

cases: Issued/revoked start remains incomplete across 120 seconds of virtual time, delayed delivery and delayed release.
Never-issued and known-failed launches complete without waiting for impossible delivery.
Claimed startup requires exact owner cleanup; duplicate/mismatched claims and a late failure cannot stand in for release.
One hundred completed lifecycles retire immediately; stale completion cannot retire a replacement.
